title: High CPU from an unknown process
symptom: PC fans spin constantly and Task Manager shows an unfamiliar process using lots of CPU
user_description: My computer is hot and noisy. Task Manager shows a process called something I don't recognise using nearly all the processor.

options.text: End every process that uses a lot of CPU, including system ones
options.why: Ending system processes can crash the PC or make it unstable. Never end things you do not understand.

options.text: Delete the program's file straight away
options.why: It may be a legitimate or system file, and deleting it destroys evidence if it is malicious. Identify it first.

options.text: Identify the process, check its publisher and file location, decide whether it is legitimate, and escalate to security if it looks suspicious
options.why: Not every unknown name is bad, so identify before acting. The file location and publisher help you tell a normal program from malware, and anything suspicious goes to the security team.

options.text: Ignore it, because it is probably normal
options.why: A process at constant full CPU is not normal. It could be a misbehaving program or malware, so it needs checking.

hints: How can you find out what a process is before you decide what to do?
What does the file location of a process tell you?
When should someone other than you get involved?
real_world_tip: Right-click the process in Task Manager and use Open file location. A strange folder is a red flag.
